html:
The Novgorod Republic was a merchant state in northern Russia, run from the city of Novgorod on the Volkhov river, from 1136 to 1478. On the map for 1279 to 1400 it covers a huge belt of forest from the Baltic to the Urals.

Novgorod was one of the oldest towns of Kievan Rus. In 1136 its people threw out their prince, and from then on princes served at the town's pleasure. Real power lay with the veche, a town assembly, and with the elected mayor and archbishop. Its wealth came from furs gathered across the northern forests and sold to the German merchants of the Hanseatic League, who kept a trading post in the city. Thousands of birch bark letters dug up there show ordinary townspeople writing to each other.

Prince Alexander Nevsky beat the Swedes on the Neva in 1240 and German knights on the ice of Lake Peipus in 1242. The Mongols never sacked the city, but it paid tribute to the Golden Horde. In 1478 Ivan III of Moscow annexed it and carried off the bell that called the veche.
